paper.title: SEFRQO: A Self-Evolving Fine-Tuned RAG-Based Query Optimizer
paper.central_claim: SEFRQO, a fine-tuned LLM query-hint generator whose prompt is rebuilt each iteration from a continually updated vector DB of execution records (similar queries + the query's own best plan and gain), self-evolves from execution feedback and outperforms PostgreSQL, Bao and Balsa: up to 65.05% (CEB) and 93.57% (Stack) latency reduction vs PostgreSQL.

signatures.operation: LLM emits a full-plan or join-order hint -> execute on PostgreSQL -> if faster than stored best, replace record -> recompute eta -> rebuild prompt for next iteration

gap.author_gap: Existing LQOs capture at most two of {learn from mistakes, no cold start, adapt to workload/schema change}; LLM optimizers cannot update cheaply at runtime.
gap.checked_gap: The runtime-learning gap for LLM optimizers is real, but 'no cold start' is not delivered by the evidence (first-iteration plans have higher RET; gains accrue over tens of repeated executions) and the per-query best-so-far memory is a repeated-execution search, not cross-query learning.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A JOB-fine-tuned LLaMA hint generator whose prompt is rebuilt from execution records (own best plan, gain, k similar queries) lowers total CEB latency by about 50-60% versus PostgreSQL when the same queries are executed 50 times and the best result per query is kept; the reference part adds about 9 points (NR ablation). Not shown: gains on unseen queries, advantage over equal-execution no-memory resampling, QGRPO benefit, 'no cold start', or superiority over Bao/Balsa on Stack overall.

G.reason: Concrete, real gap (LLM optimizers cannot learn from execution at runtime; retraining on shifts) with Bao/Balsa/LLMSteer as measured neighbours; but 'no cold start' is not demonstrated (gains accrue over repeated executions; first-iteration plans have higher RET) and the new object (per-query best memory) is a repeated-search record rather than a cross-query learner; LLM-QO/LLMOpt not run.

M.reason: Operation, information and rule are clearly specified (record replacement by measured latency, prompt with best plan + gain + k references) and some tested predictions exist (join-order-only mostly copies the default plan, too many references hurt); causal story that the LLM reasons over the feedback rather than resamples is not tested.

X.reason: Retention is gated by an external measurement with implicit rollback to best-so-far, fallback to default plan on invalid hints, next-round reading is explicit, failure/scope boundaries (drift, OLAP-only, RL variance) are stated; no staleness/invalidation for drifted records and no versioning.

E.measurement.reason: Ground-truth engine latency on PostgreSQL 16.4 with timeouts and per-iteration RET curves is a trustworthy verifier; presentation choices (best-over-iterations Table 1, filtered gains in the abstract) inflate headline numbers but per-iteration and overall metrics are also shown.

E.causality.reason: Useful ablations (fine-tuning ladder, join-order-only, no references, k, similarity) but no feedback-off control at equal execution count, no best-of-N/random-hint baseline, and the effect of the own-best/gain channel is never isolated from re-sampling; single runs.

E.holdout.reason: The retained store is built and evaluated on the same repeated queries and Table 1 takes the best of 50 iterations; JOB->Stack is a real holdout only for the fine-tuned weights, not for the VecDB claim; CEB shares the IMDB schema with JOB without overlap audit.

E.statistics.reason: Sample sizes (queries per template) and some negative results (QGRPO no gain, drift spikes, unstable 3B) are reported, but no repeated runs, intervals or fine-tuning seeds, and best-of-N selection of noisy single-run latencies is untreated.

E.cost.reason: Inference (236 ms) and retrieval (0.7 ms) overheads and the baseline iteration budget (Bao/Balsa 50 iterations) are reported; the cost of 50 repeated executions per query versus one PostgreSQL run, of fine-tuning, and a compute-matched no-memory baseline are missing.
